title.text: Two solutions that look the same

runs.text: Ana and Beto solved the pizza problem. Ana wrote
. With 23 people, both show 9. With which of these numbers of people do they give different results?
just in case something is left over
. When the division is exact nothing is left over, and he orders one pizza too many. Any number of people whose slices divide exactly by 8 breaks his solution.
It is the first contact with the idea of looking for the case that breaks a solution, which lesson 0.4 develops. Ask the group for another number that also breaks it: 8, 24 or 32.

justification.text: With 23 both show 9: it is exactly the case they already tried.
That is 48 slices, an exact division: Ana orders 6 and Beto orders 7, one too many.
That is 90 slices: Ana orders 12 and so does Beto, because slices are left over.
That is 141 slices: both order 18, because the division is not exact.
